data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 7ecf22ffdf0caa123d86ba9df17b478671fd2a7a
* **Plugin component:** plugins/dso/hooks/lib/test-result-processor.sh, function _process_test_result, TS/TSX branch
* **Consuming context:** the test-status recorder script invokes test-result-processor.sh which invokes jest CLI; downstream pre-commit-test-gate.sh blocks commit on the fabricated failure
* **Affected ecosystem:** Next.js App Router, SvelteKit, Remix, TanStack Router, and any JS framework using bracket-segment dynamic routes ([id], [locale], [projectSlug], etc.) with co-located tests

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior (reported from a host project: parity-scan)

#### Expected Behavior

The recorder should record a passing status when a Jest test file passes, regardless of whether the test path contains regex-special characters such as brackets. The Jest CLI exposes --runTestsByPath since 24.x precisely for this case: it interprets each positional arg as an exact filesystem path, not a regex. Plugin code that knows it has an exact path should use that flag.

#### Actual Behavior

The TS/TSX branch in plugins/dso/hooks/lib/test-result-processor.sh (function _process_test_result) runs:

```
elif [[ "$test_file" == *.ts ]] || [[ "$test_file" == *.tsx ]]; then
    npx --no-install jest "$full_test_path" --no-coverage >"$test_output_file" 2>&1 || exit_code=$?
```

Jest CLI semantics: positional arguments are regex patterns matched against test file paths, not exact paths. When $full_test_path is e.g. /Users/.../src/app/api/import-jobs/[id]/progress/route.test.ts, Jest treats [id] as a regex character class matching a single 'i' or 'd' — not the literal string [id]. The compiled pattern does not match any path on disk. Jest exits 1 with:

```
Pattern: /...src/app/api/import-jobs/[id]/progress/route.test.ts - 0 matches
No tests found, exiting with code 1
```

The test-status recorder reads exit 1, marks the test as failed, and writes failed_tests=<path> into $ARTIFACTS_DIR/test-gate-status. pre-commit-test-gate.sh reads that and blocks the commit on a fictitious failure.

### 3. Action History

Reproducer (any project with TS/TSX test files under bracket-named directories):

```
# What the recorder runs internally — fails:
npx --no-install jest "src/app/api/import-jobs/[id]/progress/route.test.ts"
# -> Pattern: ... - 0 matches; exit 1

# Same test, brackets escaped — passes:
npx --no-install jest "src/app/api/import-jobs/\[id\]/progress/route.test.ts"
# -> Test Suites: 1 passed
```

In the reporter's project (parity-scan), affected paths include:

- src/app/api/import-jobs/[id]/progress/route.test.ts
- src/app/api/projects/[id]/route.test.ts
- src/app/api/projects/[id]/members/route.test.ts
- src/app/api/projects/[id]/members/[email]/route.test.ts
- src/app/[locale]/[projectSlug]/...

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The shell branch (*.sh) and Python branch (*.py) of _process_test_result are not affected — bash and pytest accept positional args as filesystem paths, not regex. Only the Jest branch has this bug; symptoms are confined to TS/TSX with bracket-segment paths.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **File**: plugins/dso/hooks/lib/test-result-processor.sh, function _process_test_result, TS/TSX branch
* **Caller chain**: the test-status recorder -> test-result-processor.sh; husky pre-commit-test-gate.sh -> reads test-gate-status
* **RECORD_TEST_STATUS_RUNNER override**: workaround at the host-project level; honored by the recorder but NOT by pre-commit-test-gate.sh — so the husky gate still fires on fabricated failures even when the host has wrapped the recorder

### 6. Investigation Hints

#### Recommended fix (one-line)

Replace the positional argument with --runTestsByPath, which has been Jest's documented exact-path flag since 24.x:

```
elif [[ "$test_file" == *.ts ]] || [[ "$test_file" == *.tsx ]]; then
    npx --no-install jest --runTestsByPath "$full_test_path" --no-coverage >"$test_output_file" 2>&1 || exit_code=$?
```

--runTestsByPath interprets each positional arg as an exact filesystem path. No escaping needed — brackets, dots, parentheses, plus all work literally. Behavior on non-bracketed paths is unchanged (still resolves to exact file).

Alternative (less preferred) fixes:
- Regex-escape the path before passing as positional (functional but uses regex semantics for what should be exact-path lookup).
- Use --testPathPattern with ^...$ anchors plus escaping (same downside, more typing).

#### Severity rationale

- Failure mode silently fabricates test failures and blocks the commit; the user sees failed_tests=<file> and reasonably concludes their test broke. Diagnosing requires reading plugin internals and knowing Jest CLI regex semantics — high discovery cost.
- Affected projects: every Next.js / SvelteKit / Remix / TanStack Router project on conventional dynamic-route patterns with co-located tests. The reporter's CLAUDE.md invariant explicitly mandates project-scoped features under [projectSlug]/, so this is the unavoidable case for many host projects, not a fringe pattern.
- Workaround (RECORD_TEST_STATUS_RUNNER wrapper) is partial: it doesn't reach the husky pre-commit path. Full fix requires upstream change.
data.title: [test-result-processor]: jest TS/TSX path with brackets passed as positional regex arg -> 'No tests found' exit 1, recorder logs fabricated failure
